path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 431. Application
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 431. Application
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 431. Application (2023)
content:
Every person applying for public assistance shall be required to sign a statement
   setting forth his financial status and such other facts as may be required by the
   department, in order to determine whether such person is entitled to public assistance.  Every such applicant shall make affidavit that the facts set forth in such statement
   are true and correct.  Every person employed in the administration of public assistance shall have power
   to administer oaths for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this
   section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.4. Identification and proof of residence
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.4. Identification and proof of residence
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.4. Identification and proof of residence (2023)
content:
(a) All persons applying for assistance shall provide acceptable identification and
      proof of residence.  A person shall be deemed to be a resident when he or she documents his or her residency
      and that residency is verified by the department.  Verification may include, but is not limited to the production of rent receipts,
      mortgage payment receipts, utility receipts, bank accounts or enrollment of children
      in local schools.  General assistance applicants must establish that they have been residents of the
      Commonwealth for at least twelve months immediately preceding their application and
      they are not receiving assistance from any other state.  General assistance applicants shall disclose, in their application, all states in
      which they have resided and in which they have collected a form of public assistance
      in the last five years.  The provisions of this subsection shall not apply to General Assistance applicants
      who can establish that they moved to this Commonwealth to escape an abusive living
      situation.  The department shall adopt rules governing the proof required to establish that
      the applicant has moved to this Commonwealth to escape an abusive living situation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.12. Determination of need
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.12. Determination of need
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.12. Determination of need (2023)
content:
(a) In determining need for aid to families with dependent children, the gross income
      of all members of the assistance group who are fourteen years of age or older shall
      be considered except the gross income of a member of the assistance group who is between
      the ages of fourteen and twenty-one, is a full or part-time student, and is not employed
      full time or income which is specifically excluded by Federal or State law.  Fifty percent of gross earned income shall be disregarded when determining eligibility
      for recipients.  Any changes to that percentage shall be promulgated as regulations and shall be
      subject to the availability of Federal and State funds for cash assistance, as certified
      by the Secretary of the Budget.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.5. Resources
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.5. Resources
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.5. Resources (2023)
content:
(a) Real and personal property which an applicant or recipient owns or in which he
      or she has an interest are resources which must be considered in determining initial
      and continuous eligibility for assistance, subject to the limitations and exceptions
      hereinafter proscribed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(d) County Boards; Powers and Duties›PA ST 62 P.S. § 425. Furnishing information
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (d) County Boards; Powers and Duties › PA ST 62 P.S. § 425. Furnishing information
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 425. Furnishing information (2023)
content:
Upon request by any adult resident of the Commonwealth, any county board shall furnish
   the address and amount of assistance with respect to persons receiving assistance
   about whom inquiry is made, but such information shall not be used for commercial
   or political purposes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.3. Failure to comply with employment and work-related activity requirements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.3. Failure to comply with employment and work-related activity requirements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.3. Failure to comply with employment and work-related activity requirements (2023)
content:
(a) An applicant or recipient who is not exempt from participation in the employment
      or work-related activity requirements set forth in section 405.1(a.2)1and who without good cause:  (i) voluntarily terminates employment or reduces earnings;
      (ii) fails to apply for work at such time and in such manner as the department may
      prescribe;  or (iii) fails or refuses to accept referral to and participate in a work-related
      activity, or refuses to accept referral to and work in and retain employment in which
      the applicant or recipient is able to engage, provided such employment conforms to
      the standards established for a bona fide offer of employment, shall be disqualified
      from receiving assistance as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.13. Income averaging
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.13. Income averaging
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.13. Income averaging (2023)
content:
For purposes of determining eligibility for assistance, the income of any person under
   a contract of employment on an annual basis who works and receives income from such
   contract in fewer than twelve months, but more than eight months, shall be prorated
   over the period of the contract.  This provision shall apply only to such persons whose annual income, when averaged
   over a twelve-month period, is expected to be in excess of that set forth in the minimum
   basic standards of adequate care for the appropriate number of persons dependent upon
   such income.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.17. Timely and adequate notice defined
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.17. Timely and adequate notice defined
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.17. Timely and adequate notice defined (2023)
content:
The department shall provide timely and adequate notice in all cases of intended action
   to discontinue, terminate, suspend or reduce an assistance grant except in those cases
   where adequate notice alone would be consistent with the requirements of Federal law
   or regulation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.16. Recoupment of prior overpayments and retroactive correction of underpayments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.16. Recoupment of prior overpayments and retroactive correction of underpayments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.16. Recoupment of prior overpayments and retroactive correction of underpayments (2023)
content:
(a) In accordance with Federal law and regulations, the department shall establish
      procedures for recoupment of prior overpayments.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.23. Verification system
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.23. Verification system
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.23. Verification system (2023)
content:
(a) The department shall establish a computerized income eligibility verification
      system to verify eligibility, eliminate duplication of assistance and deter fraud:
      Provided, however, that the department, in good faith, attempts to obtain the cooperation
      by Federal authorities or other states, or both;  and further provided, that the data
      be accessible by the department.  Subject to section 432.19,1prior to authorizing assistance under section 432.2(b)2or continuing assistance under section 432.2(c), the department shall match the social
      security number of each applicant and recipient with the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.14. Reporting responsibility
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.14. Reporting responsibility
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.14. Reporting responsibility (2023)
content:
(a) It shall be the duty of the department to insure that every applicant for, or
      recipient of, assistance be notified not less frequently than semiannually as to the
      provisions of eligibility and his responsibility for reporting information concerning
      changes in circumstances which may affect the amount of grant.  After such notification has been provided, the department shall require the recipient
      to formally acknowledge, on a form prescribed for such purpose, that the provisions
      of eligibility and reporting obligations have been explained to him and were understood.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.21. Requirement that certain federal benefits be primary sources of assistance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.21. Requirement that certain federal benefits be primary sources of assistance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.21. Requirement that certain federal benefits be primary sources of assistance (2023)
content:
(a) All recipients or applicants for assistance in this Commonwealth shall cooperate
      with the department in identifying the eligibility of such recipients or applicants
      for Federal Social Security Supplemental Security Income (SSI), Federal Social Security
      Retirement, Survivor's and Disability Income benefits (RSDI) or other Federal programs
      as the primary source of financial assistance for such persons.  Any person who, without good cause, fails to cooperate with the department in an
      effort to establish such person's eligibility for SSI, RSDI or other Federal benefits
      shall have his assistance terminated, or if he has not previously received assistance,
      shall thereby be rendered ineligible for such assistance for a period of sixty days
      by reason of his noncooperation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.18. Assistance payments; lost, stolen, destroyed or not received
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.18. Assistance payments; lost, stolen, destroyed or not received
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.18. Assistance payments; lost, stolen, destroyed or not received (2023)
content:
In the event that a recipient of assistance does not receive an assistance check,
   or if such check is lost, stolen or destroyed after receipt but before it is cashed,
   the county office after a period of three days may authorize a one-time grant from
   the county disbursement, provided that the following conditions are met:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.19. Verification of eligibility
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.19. Verification of eligibility
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.19. Verification of eligibility (2023)
content:
All conditions of eligibility for assistance shall be verified prior to authorization
   of assistance or during a redetermination of a recipient's eligibility unless the
   verification is pending from a third party and the applicant has cooperated in the
   verification attempt in accordance with department standards or unless certification
   of cooperation is pending with the domestic relations section pursuant to section
   432.6.1Initial authorization of assistance shall not be delayed more than thirty days after
   application.  If the applicant establishes eligibility, assistance will be initially authorized
   effective with the date that all conditions of eligibility are verified.  Except when prohibited by Federal law, it shall be a condition of eligibility for
   assistance that an applicant or recipient consent to the disclosure of information
   about the age, residence, citizenship, employment, applications for employment, income
   and resources of the applicant or recipient which is in the possession of third parties.  Such consent shall be effective to empower any third party to release information
   requested by the department.  Except in cases of suspected fraud, the department shall attempt to notify the applicant
   or recipient prior to contacting a third party for information about that applicant
   or recipient.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.15. Quarterly earnings determination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.15. Quarterly earnings determination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.15. Quarterly earnings determination (2023)
content:
The department shall transmit to the Office of Employment Security the social security
   number of all persons over sixteen years of age who receive assistance during the
   second prior quarter.  The Office of Employment Security shall determine the amount of wages reported by
   employers for the amount of unemployment compensation insurance benefits which have
   been paid during the second and third prior quarters to persons with those social
   security numbers and shall return such information, excluding zero wage reports, to
   the department.  The department shall compare such wage reports with earnings reported by recipients,
   take prompt action to resolve discrepancies, and shall refer promptly for investigation
   any cases of suspected fraud.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.24. Eligibility for persons with drug-related felonies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.24. Eligibility for persons with drug-related felonies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.24. Eligibility for persons with drug-related felonies (2023)
content:
(a) To the extent permitted by Federal law, a person who is otherwise eligible to
      receive public assistance shall not be denied assistance solely because he has been
      convicted of a felony drug offense, provided:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.20. Prohibition on grant or assistance for moving costs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.20. Prohibition on grant or assistance for moving costs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.20. Prohibition on grant or assistance for moving costs (2023)
content:
The department shall not provide in any manner specific grants or assistance to any
   person to pay for or offset the cost of such person's moving expenses, except when
   the move is necessary to secure gainful permanent employment or is required due to
   a verifiable health reason.  Assistance shall not be provided to any assistance unit for more than one move in
   any twelve-month period, and shall not exceed two hundred dollars ($200).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.25. Eligibility for individuals convicted of drug distribution
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.25. Eligibility for individuals convicted of drug distribution
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.25. Eligibility for individuals convicted of drug distribution (2023)
content:
(a)(1) Notwithstanding sections 405.1 and 432.24, to the extent permitted by Federal
         law, no individual who, after the effective date of this section, has been convicted
         under section 13(a)(14), (30) or (37) of the act of April 14, 1972 (P.L. 233, No.
         64),1known as “The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act,” when the amount
         of controlled substances involved is equivalent to or greater than the amount of controlled
         substances set forth in18 Pa.C.S. § 7508(a)(1)(iii), (2)(iii), (3)(iii), (4)(iii), (7)(iii) or (8)(iii)(relating to drug trafficking sentencing and penalties) while receiving public assistance
         shall be eligible for public assistance unless:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 433. Special eligibility provision
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 433. Special eligibility provision
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 433. Special eligibility provision (2023)
content:
No person shall be rendered ineligible for public assistance solely by reason of his
   receiving care in a foster home or public nursing home under the provisions of acts
   relative to the powers and duties of counties or of county institution districts.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.26. Eligibility for violators of sexual offender registration
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.26. Eligibility for violators of sexual offender registration
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 432.26. Eligibility for violators of sexual offender registration (2023)
content:
Subject to Federal approval, an individual required to register as a convicted sexual
   offender pursuant to42 Pa.C.S. § 9799.13(relating to applicability) who is not compliant with the registration requirements
   imposed upon the individual by42 Pa.C.S. §§ 9799.15(relating to period of registration), 9799.19 (relating to initial registration)
   and 9799.25 (relating to verification by sexual offenders and Pennsylvania State Police)
   shall not be eligible for assistance until the individual can prove compliance with
   the applicable registration requirements.  The eligibility for assistance of minor children living in the household shall not
   be affected by an individual being deemed ineligible for assistance by this section.  The department may promulgate regulations necessary to effectuate compliance with
   the registration requirements for individuals it considers transient or homeless to
   include any address or location where public assistance funds are to be sent on behalf
   of an eligible individual.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 434. Diminishment of welfare payment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 434. Diminishment of welfare payment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 434. Diminishment of welfare payment (2023)
content:
To the extent permitted by Federal law and regulations, assistance granted under this
   article shall be diminished by amounts the recipient obtains by cashing an assistance
   check at a gambling casino, racetrack, bingo hall or other establishment which derives
   more than fifty percent of its gross revenues from gambling.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 434.2. Prohibition against duplicate payments and expedited authorization
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 434.2. Prohibition against duplicate payments and expedited authorization
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 434.2. Prohibition against duplicate payments and expedited authorization (2023)
content:
In no case shall duplicate payments be made on behalf of an aid to families with dependent
   children or general assistance child.  Notwithstanding any provision of this act, a child, formerly in the custody of a
   parent or other caregiver who is no longer exercising care and control of the child,
   shall be eligible for expedited authorization of cash assistance benefits.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 434.1. Agreements with Federal authorities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 434.1. Agreements with Federal authorities
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 434.1. Agreements with Federal authorities (2023)
content:
The department is authorized to enter into agreements with Federal authorities for
   the Federal administration of the State supplemental assistance program.  If required for Federal administration the department may make payments of the State's
   obligation with regard to State supplemental assistance prior to the month in which
   payments to eligible individuals will be made by the Federal authorities.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 435. Care by other public bodies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 435. Care by other public bodies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 435. Care by other public bodies (2023)
content:
Notwithstanding any other provisions of law, no public body shall provide without
   charge any maintenance, care or service which an individual is entitled to receive
   as assistance under the provisions of this article but this section shall not be construed
   to preclude any such public body from supplementing such assistance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 437. Reports to General Assembly
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 437. Reports to General Assembly
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 437. Reports to General Assembly (2023)
content:
Two copies of all reports required by the national center for social statistics of
   the Department of Health, Education and Welfare shall be furnished to the Senate Public
   Health and Welfare Committee and the Health and Welfare Committee of the House of
   Representatives when they are submitted to the Federal Government.  Similar reports prepared concerning general assistance, the State Blind Pension
   and State supplemental assistance shall be similarly furnished to the committees.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.5. Penalty period for asset transfer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (f) Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.5. Penalty period for asset transfer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.5. Penalty period for asset transfer (2023)
content:
(a) Pursuant to section 1917(c) of the Social Security Act (49 Stat. 620,42 U.S.C. § 1396p(c)), the department shall impose a penalty of ineligibility for all ineligible days,
      whether for full months or for a partial month's period of ineligibility, or both,
      when an applicant, recipient or spouse of an applicant or a recipient of the services
      set forth in subsection (b) transfers assets for less than fair market value within
      or after the look-back period as defined in section 1917(c) of the Social Security
      Act.  Transfers totaling five hundred dollars ($500) or less in a calendar month shall
      not be subject to the penalty.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 436. Repayments of State supplemental assistance not required; relative contributions not necessary for eligibility determination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (e) Assistance Other Than Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 436. Repayments of State supplemental assistance not required; relative contributions not necessary for eligibility determination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 436. Repayments of State supplemental assistance not required; relative contributions not necessary for eligibility determination (2023)
content:
Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no repayment shall be required of any
   State supplemental assistance paid to any person for which he was eligible;  and with
   respect to the determination of eligibility for such assistance, no relative shall
   be required to contribute to the cost of such assistance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.3. Use of medical expenses to establish eligibility for medical assistance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (f) Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.3. Use of medical expenses to establish eligibility for medical assistance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.3. Use of medical expenses to establish eligibility for medical assistance (2023)
content:
Notwithstanding any other provision of law to the contrary, in determining eligibility
   for retroactive and prospective medical assistance, only medical expenses incurred
   on or after the first day of the third month before the month of application may be
   deducted from countable income, provided that the expenses were not previously deducted
   in determining eligibility for medical assistance and are not subject to payment by
   another party, including medical assistance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.6. Treatment of life estates, annuities and other contracts in determining medical assistance eligibility
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (f) Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.6. Treatment of life estates, annuities and other contracts in determining medical assistance eligibility
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.6. Treatment of life estates, annuities and other contracts in determining medical assistance eligibility (2023)
content:
(a) As a condition of eligibility for medical assistance, every applicant or recipient
      who owns a life estate in property with retained rights to revoke, amend or redesignate
      the remainderman must exercise those rights as directed by the department.  The acceptance of medical assistance shall be an assignment by operation of law
      to the department of any right to revoke, amend or redesignate the remainderman of
      a life estate in property.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.8. Eligibility for home- and community-based services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (f) Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.8. Eligibility for home- and community-based services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.8. Eligibility for home- and community-based services (2023)
content:
As a condition of eligibility for home- and community-based services, an applicant
   shall be subject to all medical and financial eligibility requirements for medical
   assistance including:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.7. Income for the community spouse
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (f) Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.7. Income for the community spouse
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.7. Income for the community spouse (2023)
content:
(a) When a community spouse has income below the monthly maintenance needs allowance
      as determined under the department's regulations and Title XIX of the Social Security
      Act (49 Stat. 620,42 U.S.C. § 1396 et seq.), the institutionalized spouse may transfer additional resources to the community
      spouse only in accordance with this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.4. Reasonable limits on allowable income deductions for medical expenses when determining payment toward the cost of long-term care services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (f) Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.4. Reasonable limits on allowable income deductions for medical expenses when determining payment toward the cost of long-term care services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.4. Reasonable limits on allowable income deductions for medical expenses when determining payment toward the cost of long-term care services (2023)
content:
(a) When determining a recipient's payment toward the cost of long-term care services,
      long-term care medical expenses incurred six months or more prior to application for
      medical assistance shall be disallowed as a deduction, and medical and remedial expenses
      that were incurred as a result of a transfer of assets penalty shall be limited to
      zero unless application of these limits would result in undue hardship.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.1. Persons eligible for medical assistance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (f) Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.1. Persons eligible for medical assistance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.1. Persons eligible for medical assistance (2023)
content: (a) The following persons shall be eligible for medical assistance:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.9. Verification of eligibility

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.2. Medical assistance eligibility
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (f) Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.2. Medical assistance eligibility
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 441.2. Medical assistance eligibility (2023)
content:
Medical assistance shall not be granted to or in behalf of any person who disposed
   of his real or personal property, of the value of five hundred dollars ($500), or
   more, without fair consideration, within two years immediately preceding the date
   of application for medical assistance unless he is eligible for State supplemental
   assistance or unless he can clearly show that the transfer was not primarily for the
   purpose of acquiring or retaining eligibility for assistance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 443.4. Additional services for eligible persons other than the medically needy
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (f) Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 443.4. Additional services for eligible persons other than the medically needy
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 443.4. Additional services for eligible persons other than the medically needy (2023)
content:
Except for the medically needy, persons eligible for medical assistance may, pursuant
   to regulations of the department, also receive dental services, vision care provided
   by a physician skilled in diseases of the eye or by an optometrist prescribed medications,
   prosthetics and appliances, ambulance transportation, skilled nursing home care for
   an unlimited period of time, and other remedial, palliative or therapeutic services
   prescribed by or provided under the direction of a physician or podiatrist.

content:

      in subsection (b), the department shall make an eligibility redetermination every

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 443.5. Prepayment for contracted medical services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (f) Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 443.5. Prepayment for contracted medical services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 443.5. Prepayment for contracted medical services (2023)
content:
For categorically needy or medically needy persons eligible for medical assistance,
   prepaid capitation payments or insurance premiums for services under the medical assistance
   State plan may be made on behalf of eligible persons through competitive bidding with
   profit or non-profit contractors, insurers, or health maintenance organizations.  Profit and non-profit insurers must be approved under applicable State laws.  Prepaid capitation or premium payments made under such contracts shall not exceed
   payments made to other third party payers for comparable services and similar benefit
   conditions.  Capitation payments charged for anticipated medical assistance eligible persons
   under a contract may be prepaid by the Commonwealth subject to monthly, quarterly,
   and annual adjustment by the department based on actual enrollment and fixed capitation
   rates.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 443.8. Personal needs allowance deduction for medical assistance--Eligible persons in nursing facilities (2023)
content:

      clothing and other personal needs, shall be deducted from a medical assistance-eligible

      the amount that person must pay toward the cost of skilled health care and intermediate
      services or intermediate care while residing in a nursing facility.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 443.13. Emergency transportation services

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 443.13. Emergency transportation services (2023)
content:
Subject to Federal approval as may be necessary and contingent on Federal financial
   participation, from money appropriated for the department under the act of August
   3, 2023 (P.L. 471, No. 1A), known as the General Appropriation Act of 2023, sufficient
   funds shall be included to provide reimbursement for ground mileage for every loaded
   mile and to provide the greater of the highest Medicare rates published in the Ambulance
   Fee Schedule Public Use File for calendar year 2023 or the current Medicaid Ambulance
   Fees as updated by Medical Assistance Bulletin 26-22-07 effective date January 1,
   2023, beginning January 1, 2024, for services provided under the Medical Assistance--Fee-for-Service,
   Medical Assistance--Capitation and Medical Assistance--Community HealthChoices appropriations
   in the General Appropriation Act of 2023.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 444.1. Limitation on charges
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (f) Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 444.1. Limitation on charges
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 444.1. Limitation on charges (2023)
content:
As a condition of participation in the medical assistance program, vendors of services
   shall agree to accept the rates of payment authorized by this article and shall not
   seek nor accept additional payments.  The department shall permit each person eligible for assistance under this act freedom
   to choose whichever practitioner and or vendor of the services, care or prescribed
   drugs he shall desire so long as such practitioner or vendor is entitled to participate
   in the assistance program provided for in this act.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (f) Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 443.15. Medical assistance coverage for doula services

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 451. Conformity with federal legislation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 451. Conformity with federal legislation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 451. Conformity with federal legislation (2023)
content:
Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the department, with the approval of the
   Governor, may by regulation grant assistance to any persons, modify or discontinue
   any type of assistance and establish new types of assistance in order to insure receipt
   of Federal contributions for such assistance.  Any such regulation shall be void at the end of the regular session of the General
   Assembly held during the odd-numbered year next following the adoption of the regulation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 453. Expenditure of public funds for abortions limited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 453. Expenditure of public funds for abortions limited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 453. Expenditure of public funds for abortions limited (2023)
content:
Since it is the public policy of the Commonwealth to favor childbirth over abortion,
   no Commonwealth funds and no Federal funds which are appropriated by the Commonwealth
   shall be expended by any State or local government agency for the performance of abortion:
   Provided, That nothing in this act shall be construed to deny the use of funds where
   a physician has certified in writing that the life of the mother would be endangered
   if the fetus were carried to full term or except for such medical procedures necessary
   for the victims of rape or incest when such rape or incest has been reported promptly
   to a law enforcement agency or public health service.  Nothing contained in this section shall be interpreted to restrict or limit in any
   way, appropriations, made by the Commonwealth or a local governmental agency to hospitals
   for their maintenance and operation, or, for reimbursement to hospitals for services
   rendered which are not for the performance of abortions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 447. Relatives' responsibility; repayment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (f) Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 447. Relatives' responsibility; repayment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 447. Relatives' responsibility; repayment (2023)
content:
(a) Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no repayment shall be required of
      any medical assistance paid in behalf of any person for which he was eligible;  and,
      with respect to the determination of eligibility for such assistance, no relative,
      other than spouses for each other and parents for unemancipated minor children, shall
      be required to contribute to the cost of the care for which such assistance is provided.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 443.12. Nonemergency medical transportation services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (f) Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 443.12. Nonemergency medical transportation services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 443.12. Nonemergency medical transportation services (2023)
content:
(a) The department shall amend the Commonwealth's State Plan under Title XIX of the
      Social Security Act (49 Stat. 620,42 U.S.C. § 1396 et seq.) to provide nonemergency medical transportation services to eligible and enrolled
      medical assistance recipients utilizing a Statewide or regional full-risk brokerage
      model.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 444.2. Physicians' liability limited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (f) Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 444.2. Physicians' liability limited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 444.2. Physicians' liability limited (2023)
content:
Any physician rendering service as a member of a hospital utilization review committee,
   a hospital tissue committee, a health insurance review committee, a physicians' advisory
   committee, or any other committee established for the purpose of this medical assistance
   program shall not be liable for any civil damages as a result of any acts or omissions
   in rendering the service as a member of any such committee except any acts or omissions
   intentionally designed to harm or any grossly negligent acts or omissions which result
   in harm to the person receiving such service.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 449. Medical assistance pharmacy services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (f) Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 449. Medical assistance pharmacy services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 449. Medical assistance pharmacy services (2023)
content:
(a) Any managed care organization under contract to the department, or an entity with
      which the managed care organization contracts, must contract on an equal basis with
      any pharmacy qualified to participate in the Medical Assistance Program that is willing
      to comply with the managed care organization's or entity's pharmacy payment rates
      and terms and to adhere to quality standards established by the managed care organization
      or entity.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 448. Medical assistance deductible
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (f) Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 448. Medical assistance deductible
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 448. Medical assistance deductible (2023)
content:
Recipients of general assistance and general assistance-related medical assistance
   shall be responsible for a one hundred fifty dollar ($150) deductible each fiscal
   year for medical assistance-compensable ambulatory surgical center services, inpatient
   hospital services or outpatient hospital services, excluding laboratory and X-ray
   services.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 454. Medical assistance benefit packages; coverage, copayments, premiums and rates
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 454. Medical assistance benefit packages; coverage, copayments, premiums and rates
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 454. Medical assistance benefit packages; coverage, copayments, premiums and rates (2023)
content:
(a) Notwithstanding any other provision of law to the contrary, the department shall
      promulgate regulations as provided in subsection (b) to establish provider payment
      rates;  the benefit packages and any copayments for adults eligible for medical assistance
      under Title XIX of the Social Security Act (49 Stat. 620,42 U.S.C. § 1396 et seq.) and adults eligible for medical assistance in general assistance-related categories;
      and the premium or copayment requirements for disabled children whose family income
      is above two hundred percent of the Federal poverty income limit.  Subject to such Federal approval as may be necessary, the regulations shall authorize
      and describe the available benefit packages and any copayments and premiums, except
      that the department shall set forth the copayment and premium schedule for disabled
      children whose family income is above two hundred percent of the Federal poverty income
      limit by publishing a notice in the Pennsylvania Bulletin.  The department may adjust such copayments and premiums for disabled children by
      notice published in the Pennsylvania Bulletin.  The regulations shall also specify the effective date for provider payment rates.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 454.1. Case-mix rates for nursing facilities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 454.1. Case-mix rates for nursing facilities
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 454.1. Case-mix rates for nursing facilities (2023)
content:
(a) From money appropriated for medical assistance long-term living under the act
      of August 3, 2023 (P.L. 471, No. 1A), known as the General Appropriation Act of 2023,
      for fiscal year 2023-2024, the department shall calculate each nursing facility's
      case-mix rate based on the cost database and peer group prices for each net operating
      cost center used in the calculation of each nursing facility's case-mix for fiscal
      year 2022-2023.  Each nursing facility's case-mix rate shall be adjusted quarterly in accordance
      with55 Pa. Code § 1187.96(a)(5)(relating to price- and rate-setting computations).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 456. Rebates
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 456. Rebates
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 456. Rebates (2023)
content:
(a) Any Commonwealth pharmacy program that requires a manufacturer to remit a rebate
      to the program as a condition of participation shall have a clearly defined remittance
      procedure.  The procedure shall include a process for the efficient collection of rebates that
      are not in dispute and a dispute resolution process.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 459. Established drug regimens
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 459. Established drug regimens
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 459. Established drug regimens (2023)
content:
When determining prior authorization criteria for a preferred drug class, the department
   shall consider the potential destabilizing effect on the recipient's health by any
   change in the recipient's established drug regimen, including, but not limited to,
   prescription drugs for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), acquired immune deficiency
   syndrome (AIDS), behavioral health, hemophilia, hepatitis C, biologic drugs, immunosuppressants
   and anticonvulsants.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(f) Medical Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 449.2. Pharmacy benefits manager audit and obligations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (f) Medical Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 449.2. Pharmacy benefits manager audit and obligations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 449.2. Pharmacy benefits manager audit and obligations (2023)
content:
(a) The Department of the Auditor General may conduct an audit and review of a pharmacy
      benefits manager that provides pharmacy benefits management to a medical assistance
      managed care organization under contract with the department.  The Department of the Auditor General may review all previous audits completed by
      the department and shall have access to all documents it deems necessary to complete
      the review and audit.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 458. Enrollment limitation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 458. Enrollment limitation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 458. Enrollment limitation (2023)
content:
Upon enrollment in a managed care plan, an eligible person who retains eligibility
   shall maintain enrollment in the managed care plan for not less than twelve months
   unless a waiver is granted by the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(G.1) Minimum School Attendance Requirements›PA ST 62 P.S. § 463. Establishment of program
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (G.1) Minimum School Attendance Requirements › PA ST 62 P.S. § 463. Establishment of program
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 463. Establishment of program (2023)
content:
(a) Subject to Federal approval, there is established a demonstration program within
      the department to be known as the School Attendance Improvement Program.  The demonstration program shall expire three years from the date of its implementation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 460. Pharmaceutical and therapeutics committee
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 460. Pharmaceutical and therapeutics committee
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 460. Pharmaceutical and therapeutics committee (2023)
content:
(a) Any Commonwealth pharmacy program that establishes or maintains a preferred drug
      list for the purpose of receiving supplemental rebates consistent with section 1927(d)(4)
      of the Social Security Act (49 Stat. 620,42 U.S.C. § 1396r-8(d)(4)) shall establish a pharmaceutical and therapeutics committee that shall serve in
      an advisory capacity to the department and to the secretary for the purpose of developing
      and maintaining a preferred drug list.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 460.1. Drug Utilization Review Board
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 460.1. Drug Utilization Review Board
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 460.1. Drug Utilization Review Board (2023)
content:
(a) The Drug Utilization Review Board shall be established by the department consistent
      with section 1927(g)(3) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. § 1396r-8(g)(3)).  The board shall have the following powers and duties:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(G.1) Minimum School Attendance Requirements›PA ST 62 P.S. § 461. Legislative intent
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (G.1) Minimum School Attendance Requirements › PA ST 62 P.S. § 461. Legislative intent
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 461. Legislative intent (2023)
content: (a) The General Assembly finds and declares that:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(G.1) Minimum School Attendance Requirements›PA ST 62 P.S. § 466. Sanctions for failure to comply with mandatory attendance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (G.1) Minimum School Attendance Requirements › PA ST 62 P.S. § 466. Sanctions for failure to comply with mandatory attendance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 466. Sanctions for failure to comply with mandatory attendance (2023)
content:
(a) The County Board of Assistance from an area participating in the demonstration
      program shall review the school attendance of, and maintain attendance records for,
      every qualified individual subject to its jurisdiction.  When the total number of unexcused absences in any one school month exceeds three
      full days, the County Board of Assistance shall notify the qualified individual of
      the existence of an attendance problem for that school year and the possible imposition
      of sanctions under subsection (b).  This notification shall be sent by certified mail to the last known address of the
      qualified individual or the individual's parent or legal guardian, whoever is the
      primary AFDC recipient, within ten days of the review.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(G.1) Minimum School Attendance Requirements›PA ST 62 P.S. § 464. Required school attendance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (G.1) Minimum School Attendance Requirements › PA ST 62 P.S. § 464. Required school attendance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 464. Required school attendance (2023)
content:
(a) An individual who is an AFDC recipient or is a dependent child of an AFDC recipient
      from an area participating in the demonstration program shall be required to attend
      school without any attendance problems as a requirement for continuing eligibility
      for such AFDC assistance if all of the following apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(G.1) Minimum School Attendance Requirements›PA ST 62 P.S. § 462. Definitions

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 462. Definitions (2023)
content: As used in this subarticle:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(G.1) Minimum School Attendance Requirements›PA ST 62 P.S. § 469. Powers and duties of school districts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (G.1) Minimum School Attendance Requirements › PA ST 62 P.S. § 469. Powers and duties of school districts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 469. Powers and duties of school districts (2023)
content:
School districts from areas participating in the demonstration program shall be responsible
   for reporting monthly to the appropriate county assistance office of the department
   the names and other appropriate identifying information of any AFDC recipient who
   fails to meet the school attendance requirement of section 464.1In reporting attendance, the participating school district from an area participating
   in the demonstration program may not add partial days together to constitute a full
   day.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance›PA ST 62 P.S. § 459.1. Uniform Statewide preferred drug list
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (g) Special Provisions Respecting Assistance › PA ST 62 P.S. § 459.1. Uniform Statewide preferred drug list
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 459.1. Uniform Statewide preferred drug list (2023)
content:
(a) The department may not implement a uniform Statewide preferred drug list for the
      medical assistance managed care organizations until an analysis has been conducted,
      as commissioned by the department, to determine the projected cost to the medical
      assistance managed care organization and the projected supplemental rebates that could
      be obtained by the department through the use of a uniform Statewide preferred drug
      list.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(h) Fiscal Provisions›PA ST 62 P.S. § 473. Payments by federal government and political subdivisions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (h) Fiscal Provisions › PA ST 62 P.S. § 473. Payments by federal government and political subdivisions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 473. Payments by federal government and political subdivisions (2023)
content:
All payments received by the department from the United States government or political
   subdivisions of the Commonwealth for assistance or for administrative costs shall
   be paid into the State Treasury, through the Department of Revenue, and credited to
   the current appropriation made to the department for the purpose of carrying out the
   purposes of this article.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(G.1) Minimum School Attendance Requirements›PA ST 62 P.S. § 465. Qualified reasons for nonattendance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (G.1) Minimum School Attendance Requirements › PA ST 62 P.S. § 465. Qualified reasons for nonattendance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 465. Qualified reasons for nonattendance (2023)
content:
An AFDC recipient from an area participating in the demonstration program shall not
   be subject to any sanctions for nonattendance for any one of the following reasons:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(G.1) Minimum School Attendance Requirements›PA ST 62 P.S. § 468. Powers and duties of Department of Education
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (G.1) Minimum School Attendance Requirements › PA ST 62 P.S. § 468. Powers and duties of Department of Education
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 468. Powers and duties of Department of Education (2023)
content:
(a) The Department of Education, with the approval of the State Board of Education,
      shall promulgate rules and regulations to define minimum standards of attendance required
      by section 464,1to be implemented by all school districts from areas participating in the demonstration
      program to ensure meaningful participation in educational programming leading towards
      the attainment of a high school diploma or its equivalent by the AFDC recipients affected
      by the demonstration program.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(h) Fiscal Provisions›PA ST 62 P.S. § 471. Food stamp computations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (h) Fiscal Provisions › PA ST 62 P.S. § 471. Food stamp computations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 471. Food stamp computations (2023)
content:
To compute for each quarter the amount of Commonwealth funds expended by the department
   for the administration of the food stamp program for every county, and for each city
   of the first class.  For the fiscal year 1965-1966, thirty percent;  for the fiscal year 1966-1967, forty
   percent;  and, for the fiscal years 1967-1968, through 1974-1975 and the nine month
   period ending March 31, 1976, fifty percent of the amount so expended for every county,
   and for each city of the first class shall be certified to it, and shall become its
   obligation to be paid to the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(h) Fiscal Provisions›PA ST 62 P.S. § 474. Apportionment of restitution payments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (h) Fiscal Provisions › PA ST 62 P.S. § 474. Apportionment of restitution payments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 474. Apportionment of restitution payments (2023)
content:
So long as required as a condition of Federal participation, of the net amount collected
   or recovered by way of restitution from any person, or from his estate, by or for
   the department, for any assistance received to which the Federal government contributed,
   there shall be promptly paid to the United States an amount equal to its proportionate
   share of the amount collected or recovered, and the remainder thereof shall be paid
   into the State Treasury, and shall be credited to the current appropriation to the
   department, as provided by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(i) Prohibition; Penalties›PA ST 62 P.S. § 481. False statements; investigations; penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (i) Prohibition; Penalties › PA ST 62 P.S. § 481. False statements; investigations; penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 481. False statements; investigations; penalty (2023)
content:
(a) Any person who, either prior to, or at the time of, or subsequent to the application
      for assistance, by means of a wilfully false statement or misrepresentation, or by
      impersonation or by wilfully failing to disclose a material fact regarding eligibility
      or other fraudulent means, secures, or attempts to secure, or aids or abets or attempts
      to aid or abet any person in securing assistance, or Federal food stamps, commits
      a crime which shall be graded as provided in subsection (b).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(i) Prohibition; Penalties›PA ST 62 P.S. § 482. Influencing vote of recipient or applicant; penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (i) Prohibition; Penalties › PA ST 62 P.S. § 482. Influencing vote of recipient or applicant; penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 482. Influencing vote of recipient or applicant; penalty (2023)
content:
Any person employed in the administration of public assistance who, either directly
   or indirectly, influences or endeavors to influence the vote of any person receiving
   or applying for any form of assistance under the provisions of this article, shall
   be guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction thereof, shall be sentenced to pay
   a fine not exceeding one hundred dollars ($100), or to undergo imprisonment not exceeding
   six months, or both.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(i) Prohibition; Penalties›PA ST 62 P.S. § 484. Prohibited use of public assistance funds
