citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 484. Prohibited use of public assistance funds (2023)
content: (a) It shall be unlawful for any individual to:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(i) Prohibition; Penalties›PA ST 62 P.S. § 481.1. Penalty for failure to appear at criminal court proceeding
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (i) Prohibition; Penalties › PA ST 62 P.S. § 481.1. Penalty for failure to appear at criminal court proceeding
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 481.1. Penalty for failure to appear at criminal court proceeding (2023)
content:
Any person receiving any form of assistance under this article who fails as a defendant
   to appear at a criminal court proceeding when issued a summons shall be disqualified
   from receiving assistance until such time as that person complies with the summons.  The court shall cooperate with the department in the implementation of this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(l) Priority Employment Services Program›PA ST 62 P.S. § 492. Priority employment services program
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (l) Priority Employment Services Program › PA ST 62 P.S. § 492. Priority employment services program
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 492. Priority employment services program (2023)
content:
(a) The Department of Labor and Industry, through its Office of Employment Security,
      is hereby authorized to establish and provide special priority services to general
      assistance recipients above and beyond those currently available and permissible under
      Federal law, regulation and funding.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(i) Prohibition; Penalties›PA ST 62 P.S. § 483. Violation; penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (i) Prohibition; Penalties › PA ST 62 P.S. § 483. Violation; penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 483. Violation; penalty (2023)
content:
Any person knowingly violating any of the rules and regulations of the department
   made in accordance with this article shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction
   thereof, shall be sentenced to pay a fine, not exceeding one hundred dollars ($100),
   or to undergo imprisonment, not exceeding six months, or both.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(h) Fiscal Provisions›PA ST 62 P.S. § 475. Grant increases
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (h) Fiscal Provisions › PA ST 62 P.S. § 475. Grant increases
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 475. Grant increases (2023)
content:
(a) On July 1, 1982, the Department of Public Welfare shall raise general assistance
      and aid to families with dependent children allowances for assistance units of three
      or more persons by an average of at least five percent.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(i) Prohibition; Penalties›PA ST 62 P.S. § 485. Lost access devices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (i) Prohibition; Penalties › PA ST 62 P.S. § 485. Lost access devices
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 485. Lost access devices (2023)
content:
(a) A recipient who requests the replacement of an access device shall pay a replacement
      fee of five dollars ($5) for the first replacement access device requested.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(G.1) Minimum School Attendance Requirements›PA ST 62 P.S. § 467. Powers and duties of department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (G.1) Minimum School Attendance Requirements › PA ST 62 P.S. § 467. Powers and duties of department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 467. Powers and duties of department (2023)
content:
(a) Within ninety days of the effective date of this subarticle, the secretary shall
      submit to the appropriate Federal agency a request for any and all waivers of Federal
      law and regulations and for any other approvals by the Federal Government necessary
      for the implementation of this subarticle for an initial demonstration period of three
      years.  It shall be the obligation of the secretary to enter into good faith negotiations
      with the appropriate Federal officials and to make every effort to obtain the necessary
      Federal waivers and approvals.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(j) Banks and Employers to Supply Information›PA ST 62 P.S. § 488. Violation; penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (j) Banks and Employers to Supply Information › PA ST 62 P.S. § 488. Violation; penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 488. Violation; penalty (2023)
content:
(a) Any bank, industrial bank, credit union, trust company, bank and trust company,
      private banker, building and loan association, or other financial institution doing
      business in Pennsylvania, or employer who or which wilfully violates the provisions
      of section 487 of this act, or who or which wilfully makes any false or misleading
      statement in connection with any disclosure required by said section, shall be guilty
      of a misdemeanor, and upon conviction thereof, shall be sentenced to pay a fine not
      exceeding one thousand dollars ($1000).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(j) Banks and Employers to Supply Information›PA ST 62 P.S. § 489. Investigative powers and duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (j) Banks and Employers to Supply Information › PA ST 62 P.S. § 489. Investigative powers and duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 489. Investigative powers and duties (2023)
content:
(a) In furtherance of the purposes set forth in this act to prevent, deter, investigate
      and prosecute persons who have committed or are committing fraud against assistance
      programs, the department may:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(k) Employment Incentive Payments›PA ST 62 P.S. § 491. Employment incentive payments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (k) Employment Incentive Payments › PA ST 62 P.S. § 491. Employment incentive payments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 491. Employment incentive payments (2023)
content:
(a) Any corporation, bank, savings institution, company, insurance company, or mutual
      thrift institution employing persons, who prior to their employment were cash assistance
      recipients, shall be entitled to employment incentive payments to be provided as a
      credit against taxes imposed by Article IV, VII, VIII or IX of the act of March 4,
      1971 (P.L. 6, No. 2), known as the “Tax Reform Code of 1971,”1or by the act of June 22, 1964 (P.L. 16, No. 2), known as “The Mutual Thrift Institutions
      Tax Act,”2and any person, partnership or proprietorship employing such persons shall be entitled
      to payments to be provided as a credit against taxes imposed by Article III of the
      “Tax Reform Code of 1971.”  For the purposes of computing any tax liabilities against which the credit may be
      applied, deductions from taxable income shall be reduced by employment incentive payments.  Employment incentive payments unused as a tax credit in any taxable year may be
      carried over against tax liabilities of the employer in the three immediately subsequent
      taxable years.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(m) Employment Opportunities Incentive Grant Program›PA ST 62 P.S. § 493. Employment Opportunities Incentive Grant Program
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (m) Employment Opportunities Incentive Grant Program › PA ST 62 P.S. § 493. Employment Opportunities Incentive Grant Program
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 493. Employment Opportunities Incentive Grant Program (2023)
content:
(a) The Department of Labor and Industry is hereby authorized to make grants to vocational
      schools, institutions of higher learning, and commercial and nonprofit enterprises
      for the implementation of projects to provide for employment opportunities for welfare
      recipients.  These grants shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 1. Human Services Code›(j) Banks and Employers to Supply Information›PA ST 62 P.S. § 487. Information to be supplied
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 1. Human Services Code › (j) Banks and Employers to Supply Information › PA ST 62 P.S. § 487. Information to be supplied
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 487. Information to be supplied (2023)
content:
(a) Every bank, industrial bank, credit union, trust company, bank and trust company,
      private banker, and building and loan association, or other financial institutions
      doing business in Pennsylvania, shall, when requested in writing so to do by the department,
      or any county board or by any official legislative investigating committee, or by
      any authorized agent thereof, disclose to such department, board, committee, or authorized
      agent, whether or not any person applying for or receiving public assistance, or former
      recipient within four years of closing their case, or any legally responsible relative
      of such applicant or recipient, or former recipient, has had, or has any money on
      deposit with, or invested in, such banking institution or building and loan association
      within one year prior to their application for assistance, or at any time thereafter,
      the amount and date of such deposit or investment, and the amounts and dates of withdrawals
      therefrom.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.15. Jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.15. Jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.15. Jurisdiction (2023)
content:
An action authorized under the provisions of this act shall be instituted in the Commonwealth
   Court or court of common pleas in the county where the alleged unauthorized activity
   is committed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.2. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.2. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.2. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this act shall have the meanings given
   to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.3. Operation and maintenance without license prohibited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.3. Operation and maintenance without license prohibited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.3. Operation and maintenance without license prohibited (2023)
content:
No person shall maintain, operate or conduct any older adult daily living center without
   having a license issued by the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.4. License
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.4. License
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.4. License (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The department shall, after an investigation and after a departmental determination
      that the applicant complies with the provisions of this section, issue to any applicant
      a license to operate an older adult daily living center.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.1. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.1. Short title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.1. Short title (2023)
content:
This act shall be known and may be cited as the Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing
   Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.19. Bonds and costs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.19. Bonds and costs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.19. Bonds and costs (2023)
content:
No bond shall be required of and no costs shall be taxed against the department on
   account of any such action.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.6. Provisional license
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.6. Provisional license
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.6. Provisional license (2023)
content:
When there has been substantial but not complete compliance with all the applicable
   statutes, ordinances and regulations and when the applicant has taken appropriate
   steps to correct deficiencies, the department shall issue a provisional license, not
   exceeding six months, which may be renewed two times.  Upon a departmental determination of full compliance, a regular license shall be
   issued immediately.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.5. Interim license
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.5. Interim license
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.5. Interim license (2023)
content:
The department shall have the power to issue an interim license, not exceeding six
   months, to an applicant seeking to operate an older adult daily living center for
   the first time at a specified location.  The department may issue such license when it is satisfied that the applicant is
   suitable, the premises are safe and the applicant is likely to substantially comply
   with applicable regulations prior to expiration of the interim license.  Interim licenses shall not be renewable.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.9. Records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.9. Records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.9. Records (2023)
content:
Every person licensed under this act to maintain, operate and conduct a facility shall
   keep such records and make such reports as are required by the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.7. Term and content of license
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.7. Term and content of license
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.7. Term and content of license (2023)
content: A license issued by the department under this act shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.8. Right to enter and inspect
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.8. Right to enter and inspect
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.8. Right to enter and inspect (2023)
content:
(a) Inspection.--For the purpose of determining the suitability of the applicants and of the premises
      or whether or not any premises in fact qualifies as an older adult daily living center
      or the continuing conformity of the licensees to this act and to the applicable regulations
      of the department, any authorized agent of the department shall have the right to
      enter, visit and inspect any facility licensed or requiring a license under this act
      and shall have full and free access to the records of the facility and to the individuals
      and full opportunity to interview, inspect or examine such individuals.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.16. Injunction or restraining order when appeal is pending
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.16. Injunction or restraining order when appeal is pending
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.16. Injunction or restraining order when appeal is pending (2023)
content:
Whenever the department has refused to renew a license or revoked a license required
   by this act or has ordered the person to refrain from conduct violating the rules
   and regulations of the department and the person has appealed the action of the department,
   the court shall, during pendency of the appeal, issue a restraining order or injunction
   upon proof by the department that the operation of the older adult daily living center
   or its failure to comply with the order of the department is a threat to the well-being
   and safety of the adults attending the older adult daily living center.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.12. Violation; penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.12. Violation; penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.12. Violation; penalty (2023)
content:
Any person operating a facility within this Commonwealth without a license required
   by this act commits a summary offense and shall, upon conviction, be sentenced to
   pay a fine of not less than $50 nor more than $300, and costs of prosecution, and,
   in default of the payment thereof, to undergo imprisonment for not less than ten days
   nor more than 30 days.  Each day of operating a facility without a license required by this act shall constitute
   a separate offense.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.13. Actions against unlicensed older adult daily living centers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.13. Actions against unlicensed older adult daily living centers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.13. Actions against unlicensed older adult daily living centers (2023)
content:
Whenever a license is required by law for the establishment, operation or conduct
   of an older adult daily living center, the department, upon advice of the Attorney
   General, may maintain an action in the name of the Commonwealth for an injunction
   or other process restraining or prohibiting any person from establishing, conducting
   or operating any older adult daily living center during any period after a license
   to engage in such activity has been refused, has not been renewed or has been revoked
   by the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.11. Refusal to issue license; revocation; notice
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.11. Refusal to issue license; revocation; notice
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.11. Refusal to issue license; revocation; notice (2023)
content:
(a) Appeal.--Any applicant refused a license by the department shall be prohibited from conducting
      an older adult daily living center under this act.  Any appeal of that determination may be made to the department but in no event may
      an applicant commence providing older adult daily living services prior to licensure
      by the department.  The court shall enjoin, upon proof by the department, any activity by an applicant
      refused a license pursuant to this subsection.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.10. Regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.10. Regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.10. Regulations (2023)
content:
The department shall promulgate regulations to establish minimum standards for building,
   equipment, operation, care, program and services, to provide for the issuance of licenses
   and for the licensing appeal process and to establish and collect fees to offset the
   cost of issuing licenses.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.14. Actions against violations of laws and rules and regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.14. Actions against violations of laws and rules and regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.14. Actions against violations of laws and rules and regulations (2023)
content:
Whenever any person, regardless of whether such person is a licensee, has violated
   the laws of this Commonwealth pertaining to the licensing of an older adult daily
   living center or the rules and regulations adopted pursuant to such laws by the department,
   the department, upon the advice of the Attorney General, may maintain an action in
   the name of the Commonwealth for an injunction or other process restraining or prohibiting
   such person from engaging in such activity.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.17. Injunction or restraining order when no appeal is pending
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.17. Injunction or restraining order when no appeal is pending
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.17. Injunction or restraining order when no appeal is pending (2023)
content:
Should a person who is refused a license or the renewal of a license to operate or
   conduct an older adult daily living center or whose license is revoked or who has
   been ordered to refrain from conduct or activity which violates the rules and regulations
   of the department fail to appeal or should such appeal be decided finally favorably
   to the department then the court shall issue a permanent injunction upon proof that
   the person is operating or conducting an older adult daily living center without a
   license as required by law or has continued to violate the rules and regulations of
   the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.18. Search warrants
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.18. Search warrants
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.18. Search warrants (2023)
content:
Upon a showing of reasonable cause to suspect that specified premises are being used
   in violation of any provision of this act or regulations adopted pursuant thereto,
   any district justice in the district wherein the premises are located shall issue
   an administrative search warrant to any authorized agent of the department, identifying
   the premises to be searched, the scope of the search and the hours during which the
   search may be conducted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.20. Law supplementary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.20. Law supplementary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.20. Law supplementary (2023)
content:
No action brought under the provision of this act shall prevent the prosecution or
   institution of any civil or criminal action otherwise provided by law for violation
   of any law providing for licensing or departmental rules or regulations promulgated
   thereunder.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.22. Effect on issued certificates
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.22. Effect on issued certificates
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.22. Effect on issued certificates (2023)
content:
Any certificate of compliance issued by the Department of Public Welfare1with an expiration date after December 31, 1990, and before July 1, 1991, shall remain
   in effect until a licensing decision is made by the Department of Aging.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.21. Repeals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 2. Older Adult Daily Living Centers Licensing Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.21. Repeals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1511.21. Repeals (2023)
content:
Articles IX and X of the act of June 13, 1967 (P.L. 31, No. 21),1known as the Public Welfare Code, are repealed insofar as they are inconsistent with
   this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 5. Settlement by Persons Confined in Public Institutions Outside State›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1854. Inmate of public institution outside of Commonwealth cannot acquire legal settlement by establishment of residence by husband, wife, etc.
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 5. Settlement by Persons Confined in Public Institutions Outside State › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1854. Inmate of public institution outside of Commonwealth cannot acquire legal settlement by establishment of residence by husband, wife, etc.
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1854. Inmate of public institution outside of Commonwealth cannot acquire legal settlement by establishment of residence by husband, wife, etc. (2023)
content:
No person now or hereafter confined in any public institution outside of the Commonwealth
   of Pennsylvania shall acquire a legal settlement in this Commonwealth or in any county
   in this Commonwealth by virtue of the establishment of a residence in this Commonwealth
   of the husband, wife or parent or parents of the wife, husband or the minor child,
   as the case may be.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 3. Nursing Home Loan Agency Law›Article IV. General Obligation Bonds›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1521.405. Disposition and use of proceeds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 3. Nursing Home Loan Agency Law › Article IV. General Obligation Bonds › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1521.405. Disposition and use of proceeds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1521.405. Disposition and use of proceeds (2023)
content:
(a) The proceeds realized from the sale of bonds under the provisions of this act
      shall be paid into a special fund in the State treasury, hereby created, to be known
      as the “Nursing Home Loan Development Fund,” and are hereby specifically dedicated
      to the purposes of the referendum of May 21, 1974 and the referendum of November 2,
      1982 as implemented by this act.  The moneys shall be paid by the State Treasurer periodically to those departments,
      agencies, or authorities authorized to expand same at such times and in such amounts
      as may be necessary to satisfy the funding needs of the department, agency or authority.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 3. Nursing Home Loan Agency Law›Article IV. General Obligation Bonds›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1521.404. Refunding bonds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 3. Nursing Home Loan Agency Law › Article IV. General Obligation Bonds › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1521.404. Refunding bonds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1521.404. Refunding bonds (2023)
content:
The Governor, Auditor General and the State Treasurer are hereby authorized to provide,
   by resolution, for the issuance of refunding bonds for the purpose of refunding any
   bonds issued under the provisions of this act and then outstanding, either by voluntary
   exchange with the holders of such outstanding bonds, or to provide funds to redeem
   and retire such outstanding bonds with accrued interest and any premium payable thereon,
   at maturity or at any call date.  The issuance of such refunding bonds, the maturities and other details thereof,
   the rights of the holders thereof, and the duties of the Governor, Auditor General
   and the State Treasurer in respect to the same, shall be governed by the foregoing
   provisions of this act, in so far as the same may be applicable.  Refunding bonds may be issued by the Governor, Auditor General and the State Treasurer
   to refund bonds originally issued or to refund bonds previously issued for refunding
   purposes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 3. Nursing Home Loan Agency Law›Article IV. General Obligation Bonds›PA ST 62 P.S. § 1521.408. Nursing Home Loan Sinking Fund; investments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 3. Nursing Home Loan Agency Law › Article IV. General Obligation Bonds › PA ST 62 P.S. § 1521.408. Nursing Home Loan Sinking Fund; investments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 1521.408. Nursing Home Loan Sinking Fund; investments (2023)
content:
(a) All bonds issued under the authority of this article shall be redeemed at maturity
      and all interest due from time to time on such bonds shall be paid from the Nursing
      Home Loan Sinking Fund, which is hereby created.  For the specific purpose of redeeming said bonds at maturity and paying all interest
      thereon in accordance with the information received from the Governor, the General
      Assembly shall appropriate moneys to the Nursing Home Loan Sinking Fund for the payment
      of interest on said bonds and the principal thereof at maturity.  All moneys paid into the Nursing Home Loan Sinking Fund, and all of such moneys
      not necessary to pay accruing interest shall be invested by the Board of Finance and
      Revenue in such securities as are provided by law for the investment of the sinking
      funds of the Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 10. Confinement and Detention of Children›PA ST 62 P.S. § 2077. Required county detention services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 10. Confinement and Detention of Children › PA ST 62 P.S. § 2077. Required county detention services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 2077. Required county detention services (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Each county, acting alone or in conjunction with other counties as provided in section
      28,1shall by December 31, 1978, submit to the Department of Public Welfare for approval
      a plan for the removal of children from adult facilities.  If no such plan is submitted or accepted by the department within the allocated
      period, the department, after determining the detention needs of individual counties,
      shall thereafter take whatever steps it deems necessary to provide the required detention
      services for any such county or counties;  including the construction of a regional
      detention facility to meet the needs of the counties insofar as is consistent with
      prohibitions against the use of adult facilities for juvenile offenders as provided
      in Chapter 63 of Title 42 of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes (relating to juvenile
      matters).  The department, after exhausting all other available funds including Law Enforcement
      Assistance Administration funds and any other Federal or State funds available for
      such purpose, shall charge the cost of establishing the necessary regional detention
      facilities to the counties that will utilize its services.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 10. Confinement and Detention of Children›PA ST 62 P.S. § 2076. Confinement of children in jails
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 10. Confinement and Detention of Children › PA ST 62 P.S. § 2076. Confinement of children in jails
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 2076. Confinement of children in jails (2023)
content:
Until December 31, 1979, a jail may be used for the detention of a child who is alleged
   to be delinquent but only if the detention is necessary for the safety of the public
   and if the jail has been approved for the detention of the child by the Department
   of Public Welfare in good faith and the detention has been ordered by the court pursuant
   to Chapter 63 of Title 42 of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes (relating to juvenile
   matters).  The Department of Public Welfare shall approve for use for purposes of and in accordance
   with the provisions of this section any jail which it finds maintains, for the detention
   of the child, an appropriate room under adequate supervision:  Provided, That the
   Department of Public Welfare shall have, no later than October 2, 1977, by regulation
   promulgated standards governing the operations of such portions of such jails as are
   used for the detention of children pursuant to this section and shall cause the jails
   to be inspected by the Department of Public Welfare at least once every six months
   until this confinement is terminated in accordance with provisions in this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 10. Confinement and Detention of Children›PA ST 62 P.S. § 2075. Confinement of children with adults
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 10. Confinement and Detention of Children › PA ST 62 P.S. § 2075. Confinement of children with adults
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 2075. Confinement of children with adults (2023)
content:
Until December 31, 1979, a child may be detained in a facility with adults if there
   is no appropriate facility available within a reasonable distance or a contiguous
   county, whichever is nearer, for the detention of the child in which case the child
   shall be kept separate and apart from such adults at all times and shall be detained
   under such circumstances for not more than five days.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 12. Neighborhood Housing Services Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 2090.11. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 12. Neighborhood Housing Services Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 2090.11. Short title

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 12. Neighborhood Housing Services Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 2090.14. Neighborhood Housing Services Program
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 12. Neighborhood Housing Services Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 2090.14. Neighborhood Housing Services Program
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 2090.14. Neighborhood Housing Services Program (2023)
content:
There is hereby established a Neighborhood Housing Services Program to be administered
   by the department.  Its purpose shall be to create a partnership among private financial and business
   institutions, governments and residents in a given community to undertake the rehabilitation
   and revitalization of specific neighborhoods or geographical areas.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 12. Neighborhood Housing Services Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 2090.15. Powers and duties of department

(a) Grants.--The department shall provide annual grants to Neighborhood Housing Services Programs

      private sources.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare›Chapter 14. Family Preservation Act›PA ST 62 P.S. § 2174. Family Preservation Program
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 62 P.S. Poor Persons and Public Welfare › Chapter 14. Family Preservation Act › PA ST 62 P.S. § 2174. Family Preservation Program
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 62 P.S. § 2174. Family Preservation Program (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment.--The department, through grants to counties, shall establish and supervise a program,
      to be known as the Family Preservation Program, which will provide intensive intervention
      services to families whose children are at risk of immediate out-of-home placement
      under the custody of a county children and youth agency.
